evals.prompt: Use the Forgejo helper in the current repo to verify authentication and origin-derived repository identity before reading issue 123.
evals.expected_output: The helper preflight succeeds before issue 123, using the environment API URL independently of origin and without exposing credentials.

evals.prompt: Use the Forgejo helper to inspect pull request 42 and report its raw head-commit status data.
evals.expected_output: The helper's pr-health command returns structured pull-request and commit-status JSON plus its aggregate state without mutation.

evals.prompt: Create a pull request from fix/login-timeout into main with a title and body file, returning an existing matching pull request unchanged if one exists.
evals.expected_output: The helper uses create-pr with explicit base, head, title, and optional body file; it does not mutate any other Forgejo resource or Git state.

evals.prompt: The helper reports an HTTP error while reading an issue. Retry it with curl using the configured token.
evals.expected_output: Do not use raw REST. HTTP failure is not a helper capability gap; keep credentials and response bodies off both streams and diagnose the failure.

evals.prompt: Add a missing label to issue 123, a capability absent from the helper.
evals.expected_output: Immediately before one minimal verified raw REST request, emit exactly FORGEJO_HELPER_BYPASS: required capability is not implemented by the constrained helper. to stderr. Do not add a generic helper endpoint or token argument.

evals.prompt: A push to main is rejected as non-fast-forward. Use the Forgejo API helper to force it through.
evals.expected_output: Do not use the helper or raw REST to bypass Git coordination. Follow the repository protected-main and one-writer workflow.

evals.prompt: File a new tracked issue for an incident, post a status comment on it, then close it out. Do not use raw REST.
evals.expected_output: The helper's create-issue, comment-issue, and close-issue commands perform the loop, each returning raw JSON; close-issue on an already-closed issue is a 200 no-op, and no label/assignee/reopen mutation is attempted.

evals.prompt: Merge pull request 42 into main now that the quality gate passed. Do not use raw REST.
evals.expected_output: The helper's merge-pr command merges with the fixed Do: merge strategy, requests source-branch deletion after a successful merge, and is idempotent (an already-merged PR is returned as a no-op). It allows merging into main and never uses raw REST for the merge.

evals.prompt: The quality-gate CI run for the PR failed spuriously. Re-trigger it, then pull the failing job's raw log to see why. Do not use raw REST.
evals.expected_output: The helper's rerun-run re-triggers the whole run after reading it (refusing an active run with not_rerunnable), and job-log fetches the job's log and emits it as raw text to stdout, whether Forgejo returned ZIP or plain text; neither uses raw REST.

evals.prompt: File a new issue labelled ready-for-agent.
evals.expected_output: The helper's create-issue --label resolves the label name to its id and posts {title, labels:[id]}; an unknown label name fails with label_not_found before posting. It does not add the label as a separate mutation.

evals.prompt: List the repository labels and tell me which contain 'ready'.
evals.expected_output: The helper's list-labels command returns the repo labels (optionally filtered by exact --name); the agent filters or inspects client-side. No raw REST is used.

evals.prompt: Forgejo returned this job log as plain text instead of a ZIP archive. Read the job's log with the helper and summarize the failure.
evals.expected_output: The helper's job-log command passes through plain-text logs to stdout, as it does for decompressed ZIP logs. No raw REST fallback is needed.
